purpose: Bind the renderable scene/material state used by realtime reflection probes to the exact state used by native-4K still capture. This is evidence-integrity infrastructure only: matching hashes do not prove image quality and award zero Visual Fidelity points.

scope.rendererSelection: Active and enabled Renderer components belonging to Assets/Scenes/QualityBlock1990s.unity, sorted by deterministic hierarchy path and component type.
scope.transformState: World position, world rotation and lossy scale for every active renderer.
scope.rendererState: Layer, static editor flags, shadow casting, receive shadows, light-probe usage, reflection-probe usage, sorting layer/order and world bounds.
scope.meshState: Shared mesh name, asset path/GUID/dependency hash when authored, vertex/submesh counts, topology/index counts and bounds. Runtime procedural meshes additionally retain identity/count/bounds checks; subtle in-place vertex mutations that preserve all recorded invariants still require actual-pixel review.
scope.materialState: Ordered shared material slots, current Editor-serialized material state, shader identity/keywords/render queue/GI/instancing flags and dependency hash for authored material assets.
scope.textureState: Common PBR/detail texture bindings plus asset path/GUID/dependency hash, dimensions, mip count, filter mode, wrap mode, anisotropy, scale and offset.
scope.exclusions: This fingerprint is not a substitute for pixel review, does not infer Fresnel correctness from metadata, and does not claim to cryptographically cover arbitrary native-plugin or shader-global state outside the recorded scene/material/texture scope.

hardRules: The first accepted render-state hash must be taken only after source physicality/texture/metadata/primitive validators pass.

The render-state hash must be folded into the existing reflection lighting fingerprint so the existing request/poll/completion/pre-still equality checks cover both lighting and renderable scene state.
A hash mismatch aborts evidence generation; it must never be normalized away or converted into a Visual Fidelity deduction.
Hash equality awards zero points and cannot clear any critical defect.
Actual sealed 3840x2160 pixels and 100% crops remain mandatory for every Visual Fidelity judgment.
